subject: Private VPC topology, control/data plane split — topology confirmation & evidence request
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@telcoedge.com>, Anita Rao <anita@edgeops.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC topology, control/data plane split — topology confirmation & evidence request

Hi Tom / Anita,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Attached is Redwood's current draft of the private-VPC topology (v3) and a short control/data-plane matrix that maps endpoints, ports, and auth expectations. A few asks so we can finalize the SOW and the routing/KMS work: 

- Can you confirm whether control-plane traffic from the tenant will terminate at your colocated router (10.1.1.0/24) or at the cloud egress IPs? We need to know where to advertise the control-plane prefixes for BGP setup.
- Please provide the public IP ranges and any reserved ASN(s) you expect us to peer with.
- For egress: share the ACLs / firewall rules you plan to enforce (we called out example ports in the attached doc). If you already have a canonical ACL PDF, please attach.
- KMS/HSM: confirm whether you will provide an external KMS endpoint or if Redwood should use customer-managed keys in your HSM (we listed both options in the matrix).
- Compliance evidence: if you have a network boundary diagram and SOC2 or penetration-test evidence we can reference for the SOC checklist, please drop it here or point us to a Drive link.

Timeline: if we can get confirmations and the egress ACL by EOD Friday (2027-06-18), we can lock the canary cutover window for next week.

Attachments: vpc-topology-draft-v3.pdf, control-data-plane-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — short bullets preferred. I can jump on a 30m if you want to walk the diagram.

Sean Gallagher
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@telcoedge.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Rao <anita@edgeops.io>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC topology, control/data plane split — topology confirmation & evidence request

Sean — thanks. Quick answers and attached our current edge docs.

- Control-plane termination: for our initial rollout the control-plane will terminate at our colocated router (10.1.1.0/24). We are planning to announce a dedicated /29 from our ASN to avoid collisions; we'll provide the exact ASN/IP set in the follow-up.
- Public IP ranges / ASN: attaching the allocation sheet (telcoedge-egress-acls.pdf) — final allocation coming from network ops by tomorrow morning.
- Egress ACLs: see attached PDF (telcoedge-egress-acls.pdf). Notes: outbound NAT to 198.51.100.0/24, allow 443/80 to Redwood egress points, block inbound initiated connections to tenant VMs.
- KMS: for now we'll provide a customer-managed KMS endpoint (url: kms.telcoedge.local) behind the VPC peering — we will need guidance on TLS mutual auth options.
- Compliance evidence: we have a high-level net-boundary diagram included in the PDF. Full SOC2 artifacts require an NDA; happy to share limited items once legal signs off.

Attaching: telcoedge-egress-acls.pdf

Tom
Tom Jenkins
Network Architect, TelcoEdge
ton.jenkins@telcoedge.com | +1 (206) 555-2222

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Tom Jenkins <tom.jenkins@telcoedge.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC topology, control/data plane split — topology confirmation & evidence request

Sean / team — quick technical read:

- Good: terminating control-plane at Tom's colocated router reduces latency and keeps the control path separate. Confirm whether the /29 will be a dedicated peerable block (we need exact prefix to program ACLs).
- BGP: we expect to receive a static route for the control-plane /29 and then peer BGP on TCP/179 with MD5 (if TelcoEdge supports). If MD5 not available, we'll use BFD + eBGP timers tuned to 1s/3s.
- NAT/fallback: need to decide if Redwood should NAT egress from appliances (recommended) or rely on tenant NAT at TelcoEdge. Implication: if Redwood NATs, our egress IPs must be whitelisted by TelcoEdge ACLs.
- KMS TLS mTLS: for the KMS behind the peering, we recommend client certs + IP allowlist. Marcus will draft sample nginx proxy mTLS config and share.

Quick ask for Tom: can you post the exact ASN and the /29 in a follow-up? Also confirm whether you allow MD5 on BGP sessions.

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below.

Summary:
- Control-plane: TelcoEdge will terminate at colocated router; they will announce a dedicated /29 from their ASN.
- BGP: Marcus will confirm MD5 support; fallback is BFD + tuned timers.
- Egress ACLs: TelcoEdge sent ACL PDF — Redwood to confirm NATing approach.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS endpoint behind peering; Redwood to provide mTLS examples.

Action items (owners / ETA):
- Tom: share exact ASN + /29 and final ACL PDF (owner: Tom) — ETA: 2027-06-18 EOD (pending).
- Marcus: draft mTLS proxy example + BGP tune doc (owner: Marcus) — ETA: 2027-06-21.
- Irene: start the compliance packet request (NDA trigger + list of artifacts we need) and drop a Drive folder. (owner: Irene) — ETA: 2027-06-19.
- Jonas: schedule 30m cutover pre-check with TelcoEdge and our infra on 2027-06-23. (owner: Jonas)

Tom — if you can attach the finalized allocation sheet and the ACLs into the Drive link above, we'll confirm the SOW and push the DocuSign. I've created a SOW draft and linked it here: DOCUSIGN-12345.

If anything here is off, call me — otherwise we'll move to SOW signature once Tom posts the /29.

Best,
Sean
